facts.raw_span: 63-year-old man
8-month history of painless scrotal swelling
bilateral testicular enlargement without tenderness
large, solid masses in both testes
Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin, α-fetoprotein, and lactate dehydrogenase were all within normal limits
no evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses
7.0 × 6.0 × 4.2 cm tumor confined to the testis with lymphovascular invasion
pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types: small cells, medium cells, and large cells

concepts.why: The presence of a large, solid mass in the testis, lymphovascular invasion, and a pleomorphic tumor composed of multiple cell types supports this diagnosis.
The combination of a large, solid mass in the testis, lymphovascular invasion, and a tumor with multiple cell types is consistent with a mixed germ cell tumor.
The presence of a large, solid mass in the testis and lymphovascular invasion could be indicative of a yolk sac tumor, although the normal α-fetoprotein levels are not typical for this diagnosis.
The pleomorphic nature of the tumor, with multiple cell types, could suggest a teratoma, although the presence of lymphovascular invasion is not typical for this diagnosis.

The presence of a large, solid mass in the testis and lymphovascular invasion could be indicative of choriocarcinoma, although the normal β-human chorionic gonadotropin levels are not typical for this diagnosis.
The presence of a large, solid mass in the testis and lymphovascular invasion could be indicative of seminoma, although the pleomorphic nature of the tumor is not typical for this diagnosis.

The lack of evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses on the positron emission tomography–computed tomography scan rules out lymphoma as a primary diagnosis but the test was performed to evaluate for lymphoid malignancy.

rationales.F04: Bilateral testicular enlargement with large solid masses is concerning for testicular cancer, which includes embryonal carcinoma, mixed germ cell tumor, yolk sac tumor, teratoma, choriocarcinoma, and seminoma.
rationales.F05: Normal serum tumor markers decrease the likelihood of certain testicular cancers, such as choriocarcinoma, which typically presents with elevated β-human chorionic gonadotropin.
rationales.F06: The absence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses makes lymphoma less likely.
rationales.F08: A pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types is highly suggestive of a mixed germ cell tumor or another type of testicular cancer.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types and the lack of specific markers for other tumors support the diagnosis of Mixed germ cell tumor, which can contain multiple cell types, including embryonal carcinoma.
